summary: Atlas support is an organization-level paid subscription on top of usage: Basic is free, and the paid plans are Developer (30-day free trial, 8-hour initial response goal), Pro (first response from 2 hours) and Enterprise (30 minutes on the plans page, 15 minutes to 2 hours in the docs), with Platinum (15 minutes) also listed on the plans page. Neither the docs nor the plans page publishes prices; the only public formula is a January 2024 MongoDB staff forum reply (Developer the greater of $49 or 20% of total monthly charges, Pro the greater of $799 or 20%), and plan changes take effect on the first day of the next month while reactivation bills retroactively for up to 90 days. This pack draws on 5 source pages across 3 host labels and covers definitions, mechanism, parameters, how-to, measures, problems and comparisons, with 2 recorded disagreements.

facts.text: Atlas support tiers are Basic (free), Developer, Pro and Enterprise; the plans page also lists Platinum. Initial Severity-1 response goals: Developer 8 hours, Pro 2 hours, Enterprise 30 minutes, Platinum 15 minutes (the docs say Enterprise 15 min to 2 hours).

MongoDB Atlas offers several packages to support your organization or project. Atlas includes a free Basic support plan, or you can subscribe to a paid plan (Developer, Pro, or Enterprise) for extended support services. Details on support plans are available through the UI as part of the procedure to change your support plan or by contacting MongoDB.
Every Atlas user has access to free, Basic support. For teams that need faster response times and additional security features, we have a plan for you.
Only users with the Organization Owner role can change an organization's support plan. Developer has a 30-day free trial and auto-enrolls into paid Developer at the estimated cost afterwards.

Reactivating Developer or self-serve Pro after cancelling bills support retroactively from when a non-Basic plan was last active, up to 90 days back; the forum example showed a confirmation prompt adding ~$705.48 of prior charges to the pending invoice. Exceptions: Developer to self-serve Pro, and self-serve Pro to subscription-tied Pro.

On invoices, paid support appears as a monthly total in the Summary and as per-cloud-provider line items in Details, split proportionally to usage per provider; unattributed support lands under Other Atlas Usage. The support minimum is computed once per month for the whole organization.

Switching plans changes billing on the first day of the next month; canceling during a trial stops billing immediately; canceling outside a trial takes effect at month end with billing continuing until then.
If you have a paid support plan, your invoice lists the total monthly support cost in the Summary section. Support cost line items appear in the Details section.

Reactivating this support plan will retroactively charge you for support from the date a non-Basic support plan was last active (up to 90 days in the past). Support charges since September 26, 2023 (~$705.48) will be added to your current pending invoice within 24-48 hours once you click “Confirm”.

Regarding reactivation: to explain that, it’s important to understand that support is like insurance. The model is that you pay for it so that you can use it when you need it. Some (a very small number) people try to game offerings like this by turning support on and off as though it’s a one-time service, and that’s what we’re aiming to prevent here. Note that we separately offer consulting services including low-priced Flex Consulting for one-off scenarios. I want to be clear that the goal with reactivation is simply to discourage abuse. Atlas distributes support charges proportionally across the cloud providers that host your usage. The Details section lists a separate support line item for each cloud provider you use. Support usage that isn't associated with a cloud provider appears under Other Atlas Usage. Atlas calculates your support minimum once per month for your entire organization, separately from these per-provider charges.

You cancel self-serve Pro support and activate Pro support that is tied to a subscription.

Atlas schedules for the cancellation of your plan at the end of the month and your billing continues until the cancellation period.
If you cancel during a trial period, billing stops immediately. If you cancel outside of a trial period, your Atlas plan will be canceled at the end of the month and billing continues until then.

The pricing for Atlas Support can be found within the Atlas UI if you click on the Support section (left nav) of your org home.

A MongoDB staff member (Andrew Davidson, 2024-01-05) stated Atlas Developer is priced starting at $49/month, billed at the greater of $49 or 20% of total monthly charges, and Atlas Pro starts at $799/month.

Granular database auditing, customer-key encryption at rest and LDAP are paid add-ons on Developer and Pro but included in Enterprise and Platinum; the billing docs say the 15% (KMS/LDAP) and 10% (auditing) cluster uplifts exclude Enterprise and Platinum customers.

Third-party guidance says premium support typically costs up to 20% of monthly cluster spend, with negotiated rates for large enterprise deals; this is consistent with the 20% forum figure but is not an official MongoDB price.
Premium support typically costs up to 20% of monthly cluster expenses, though MongoDB offers negotiated rates for large enterprise deployments.

Excluding MongoDB Atlas Enterprise and MongoDB Atlas Platinum customers, Atlas charges a 15% uplift to the cost of each cluster with LDAP User Authentication and Authorization or Encryption at Rest using Customer Key Management enabled.

Excluding MongoDB Atlas Enterprise and MongoDB Atlas Platinum customers, Atlas charges a 10% uplift to the hourly cost of all dedicated clusters. The 10% uplift applies to projects using Database Auditing.
